text.p: McKesson Corp said Monday it completed the acquisition of the health-care distribution business of FoxMeyer Drug Co.
Under an amended agreement, McKesson paid about $23 million in cash to FoxMeyer, settled about $500 million in secured debt and assumed an additional $75 million in other liabilities.
The acquisition consisted primarily of accounts receivable and inventories of about $650 million, customer contracts and fixed assets.
The FoxMeyer acquisition will not affect McKesson's financial ability to pursue other acquisitions or share repurchases, it said.
McKesson expects to eliminate about $80 million of fixed costs during a two-and-a-half-year integration of the business.
The deal is expected to be accretive to earnings within 90 to 180 days after sufficient operating efficiencies are achieved, McKesson said.
FoxMeyer has operated as a debtor in possession under the protection of Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code. McKesson said the deal closed on November 8 after all necessary approvals.

McKesson said it would use available cash balances and its revolving credit agreements to finance the deal. The company said its investment in the FoxMeyer business after the restoration of normal credit terms was about $400 million.
